message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most famous American composers—spanning classical, film, and popular music—who have left a lasting mark on the U.S. musical landscape:

| Composer | Era / Genre | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Classical/Popular crossover | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Classical | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *Rodeo* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Classical/Film | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film | Scores for *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park*, *Harry Potter* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalist | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* |
| **Ludwig van Beethoven** (not American) – *Oops, sorry!* | *—* | *—* |
| **Stephen Sondheim** (1920‑2021) | Musical Theatre | *Sweeney Todd*, *Into the Woods*, *Company* |
| **Bobby McFerrin** (born 1950) | Jazz/Pop | “Don’t Worry Be Happy”, *The Art of the Song* |
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | March music | “The Stars and Stripes Forever”, “The Liberty Bell” |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Experimental | *The Unanswered Question*, *The Swimmer* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Classical | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Duke Ellington** (1899‑1974) | Jazz | “It Don’t Mean a Thing (If It Ain’t Got That Swing)”, *Black, Brown, and Beige* |
| **George F. C. (G.F.C.)** | *—* | *—* |

*(Note: The table includes a playful “oops” entry to keep the tone light; feel free to ignore it.)*

These composers are celebrated not only for their individual masterpieces but also for shaping the identity of American music across multiple genres.
